title: Tortilla (or Corn) Chips
summary: Corn tortillas, fried and tossed in seasoning. That’s it.
intro: **Chips are just tortillas (corn) fried and tossed in seasoning. That’s it.**

If you use store-bought tortillas, look for only two ingredients: masa and water, maybe salt. Gums and fillers are crap and likely to upset your stomach. HOWEVER, if you don’t have the skill or energy to make super-perfect tortillas at home, AND you want light, crispy chips, use store-bought machine-made tortillas.

If you want strong, thick chips for dipping thick sauces or beans, make your own tortillas. Make them thick on purpose (or by accident). “Corn” chips are just a thicker, smaller shape, like the Fritos brand.

Use a shelf-stable fat, preferably one that’s solid on the shelf: **lard, tallow, coconut.** If you use those nasty refined cooking oils, your chips will go “stale” within a few hours. Made with a stable fat, they’ll stay crispy for at least a couple of weeks.

equipment.note: A saucepan is awkward, and you need a thermometer to hold the right temperature.

stages.title: The Cook
stages.where: Fryer at {temp:320F}, or 1 stove burner on high

steps: **Slice** into shapes for chips. Stack several to make it easier.
**Fry** in batches, 7 min, stirring with a spoon until the bubbling stops.

pace.text: Have the bowl and seasoning ready: the next step comes right away.

steps: **Remove** to a bowl and toss with seasoning. If some aren’t done, just put them back in the fryer.
**Slice** into shapes. Perfect tortillas for crispy chips; thick, non-puffing ones for strong chips.
**Fry** 7 min, stirring, until the bubbling stops.
**Toss** with seasoning in a bowl. Not done? Back in the fryer.
keys: Tortillas: masa, water, maybe salt. Nothing else.
